findings.fix: Delete the declaration; downstream code needing `(nonzeroJointWeightAction N ρ).ker.FiniteIndex` gets it by `inferInstance` from `Subgroup.finiteIndex_ker`.
findings.issue: `finiteIndex_ker_nonzeroJointWeightAction` adds nothing over Mathlib's instance `Subgroup.finiteIndex_ker`: the goal is syntactically `f.ker.FiniteIndex`, so typeclass search finds it automatically (the `[Finite f.range]` argument is discharged by `Equiv.finite_right` + `Subtype.finite` from `finite_nonzeroJointWeights` above). findings.issue: `mapsTo_iInf_eigenspace_unitHom_of_nonzeroJointWeightAction_eq` is the immediately preceding `map_iInf_eigenspace_unitHom_eq_self_of_nonzeroJointWeightAction_eq` transported across `Set.MapsTo f ↑p ↑p ↔ p.map f ≤ p`, with an artificially stronger `∀ g` hypothesis (only `hχ g` is used), and its 6-line proof re-derives that transport by hand (`Submodule.mem_map_of_mem` + `rwa`).

summary: `finiteIndex_ker_nonzeroJointWeightAction` is Mathlib's `Subgroup.finiteIndex_ker` instance restated at one hom, and instance search already produces it verbatim; `mapsTo_iInf_eigenspace_unitHom_of_nonzeroJointWeightAction_eq` restates the preceding lemma through a Mathlib iff it re-derives by hand. The finiteness and finrank bound themselves are new and reuse the independence API correctly.
